Here's a structured comparison of the two documents:

---

## Purpose & Nature

| Aspect | `REQUIREMENTS.md` | `PROJECT_SPECIFICATION.md` |
|---|---|---|
| Type | Broad, open-ended requirements | Focused MVP spec for 1-week sprint |
| Date | No date | Feb 11–18, 2026 |
| Status | Ongoing reference | "Awaiting Approval" at time of writing |
| Author | Implicit (user) | AI Project Manager (GitHub Copilot) |

---

## Scope Differences

### In `REQUIREMENTS.md` but explicitly **deferred** in PROJECT_SPECIFICATION.md:
- **Cover letter generation** — full template spec in `REQUIREMENTS.md` (§4); deferred to Phase 2 Priority #3 in spec
- **Interview screening question responses** — STAR method, response strategy (§5 in REQUIREMENTS.md); deferred to Phase 2 Priority #4
- **Google Drive integration** — explicit requirement #5 in REQUIREMENTS.md; deferred in spec
- **Job application tracking** — implied by archive/metadata strategy; deferred to Priority #5
- **Analytics, LinkedIn profile, mobile, multi-user** — absent from `REQUIREMENTS.md` but named and deferred in spec

### In `PROJECT_SPECIFICATION.md` but **absent** from REQUIREMENTS.md:
- **CV Editing UI** (Priority #1) — in-browser editing, live preview, save/reset, `POST /api/edit` endpoint
- **Formal user stories** (US-1 through US-4) with acceptance criteria
- **Detailed implementation plan** — 6-day day-by-day task breakdown
- **Risk management tables** — technical and schedule risk matrices
- **Success metrics** — Must Have / Should Have / Nice to Have tiers with quality gates

---

## Technical Differences

| Area | `REQUIREMENTS.md` | `PROJECT_SPECIFICATION.md` |
|---|---|---|
| **PDF generation** | `weasyprint` / `pdfkit` (HTML→PDF) | Quarto (`quarto_generator.py`) ⚠️ *now superseded — Jinja2 HTML template used instead* |
| **DOCX generation** | `python-docx`, `mammoth`, `pypandoc` mentioned | `docx_generator.py` with `python-docx` only |
| **Semantic similarity** | `transformers` (HuggingFace) specified | Not specified; implied via LLM |
| **Frontend** | Not described | Vanilla JS + DataTables, WYSIWYG editor tab |
| **New backend modules** | Not defined | `quarto_generator.py`, `docx_generator.py`, `cv_editor.py` explicitly specified |
| **API endpoints** | None specified | Full `POST /api/edit` request/response schema |

---

## Content Depth Differences

**`REQUIREMENTS.md` is deeper on:**
- ATS formatting rules (full "What to Avoid" list, keyword placement priority)
- Human-readable CV layout specifics (exact hex colors, sidebar %, font names, page-by-page content distribution)
- Master data schema (`Master_CV_Data.json` full JSON example with tagging system)
- Cover letter template and tone-matching by employer type
- Interview response strategy with STAR format

**`PROJECT_SPECIFICATION.md` is deeper on:**
- Component architecture diagram
- Data flow sequence diagram
- Quarto template YAML/markdown structure
- ATS DOCX Python code skeleton
- Post-MVP roadmap with estimates
- Dependencies with version numbers and install instructions

---

## Key Tension / Divergence

The biggest structural divergence: **`REQUIREMENTS.md` treats cover letters, interview screening, and Google Drive as in-scope requirements**, while **`PROJECT_SPECIFICATION.md` explicitly defers all of them**. The spec is a deliberate narrowing of scope for an MVP, not a comprehensive fulfillment of REQUIREMENTS.md.

Additionally, the PDF generation approach diverged from both documents: `REQUIREMENTS.md` suggested `weasyprint`/`pdfkit`, the spec specified Quarto, and the actual implementation (per the stored memory) uses a **Jinja2 HTML template** — neither approach from either document.

**Acceptance**: PDF generated via Quarto, downloadable from UI] map[filePath:/Users/warnes/src/cv-builder/PROJECT_SPECIFICATION.md newString:### 5.2 Jinja2 HTML Template Structure

#### Template File: `templates/cv-template.html`

The template uses standard Jinja2 syntax with the `cv_data` dictionary as context:

```html
<!-- Sidebar (32% width) -->
<div class="sidebar">
  <section class="contact">
    <h2>Contact</h2>
    <p>{{ personal_info.contact.email }}</p>
    <p>{{ personal_info.contact.phone }}</p>
  </section>

  <section class="education">
    <h2>Education</h2>
    {% for edu in education %}
    <div class="edu-entry">
      <strong>{{ edu.degree }}</strong>
      <span>{{ edu.institution }}, {{ edu.end_year }}</span>
    </div>
    {% endfor %}
  </section>

  <section class="skills">
    <h2>Skills</h2>
    {% for category, data in skills.items() %}
    <h3>{{ data.category }}</h3>
    {% for skill in data.skills %}
    <span class="skill-tag">{{ skill.name }}</span>
    {% endfor %}
    {% endfor %}
  </section>
</div>

<!-- Main Content (68% width) -->
<div class="main-content">
  <h2>Professional Summary</h2>
  <p>{{ professional_summary }}</p>

  <h2>Experience</h2>
  {% for exp in experiences %}
  <div class="job-entry">
    <h3>{{ exp.title }} | {{ exp.company }}</h3>
    <span>{{ exp.start_date }} – {{ exp.end_date }}</span>
    <ul>
    {% for ach in exp.achievements %}
      <li>{{ ach.text }}</li>
    {% endfor %}
    </ul>
  </div>
  {% endfor %}
</div>
```

#### PDF Conversion: WeasyPrint (primary) / Chrome headless (fallback)

```python
# In cv_orchestrator._convert_html_to_pdf()
import weasyprint
weasyprint.HTML(filename=str(html_file)).write_pdf(str(pdf_output))
``` oldString:### 5.2 Quarto Template Structure

#### YAML Header
```yaml
---
title: "{{personal_info.name}}"
subtitle: "{{job_info.title}}"
format:
  pdf:
    template: cv-template.html
    css: cv-styles.css
    pdf-engine: chrome
    margin-top: 0.5in
    margin-bottom: 0.5in
    margin-left: 0.75in
    margin-right: 0.75in
params:
  personal_info:
    name: "Gregory R. Warnes"
    title: "Senior Bioinformatics & ML Scientist"
    email: "greg@warnes.net"
    ...
  experiences: [...]
  skills: [...]
  ...
---
```

#### Document Structure
```markdown
<!-- Sidebar (30% width) -->
::: {.sidebar}
## Contact
{{personal_info.email}}
{{personal_info.phone}}

## Education
{{#each education}}
### {{degree}}
{{institution}}, {{year}}
{{/each}}

## Skills
{{#each skills}}
- {{name}}
{{/each}}
:::

<!-- Main Content (70% width) -->
::: {.main-content}
## Professional Summary
{{summary}}

## Experience
{{#each experiences}}
### {{title}} | {{company}}
*{{start_date}} - {{end_date}}*

{{#each achievements}}
- {{this}}
{{/each}}
{{/each}}
:::
